chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: In the case of a man who said to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin,' he said, 'He is struck.' I asked, 'And if he repeats it?' He said, 'He is struck, for he will likely cease.' Yunus said, 'He is struck with a disciplinary strike, not the fixed punishment (hadd), so as not to harm a believing woman by implication (ta'rid).
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling and punishment for a husband who claims his wife was not a virgin?
ai.summary: In this hadith from the chapter of *Lian* (conjunction), Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the husband's claim of non-virginity incurs a disciplinary strike (*darb al-adab*) rather than the fixed punishment (*hadd*), ensuring the penalty is proportional and does not cause undue harm through mere implication (*ta'rid*). The ruling emphasizes that repeated strikes serve as a corrective measure to compel the husband to cease his assertion, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding excessive burden in marital disputes. This distinction highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in balancing evidentiary claims with the preservation of the wife's dignity.
